**Reading map:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), §2.7. This is an original lesson using our delivery-operations example—not reproduced textbook content.

## Why the concept matters

A linear model maps feature vectors to numerical scores. To call a mapping linear, it must preserve addition and scalar multiplication—not simply have a straight-looking plot.

## Define the mathematical relationship

$$
T(a\boldsymbol x+b\boldsymbol z)=aT(\boldsymbol x)+bT(\boldsymbol z),\qquad T(\boldsymbol x)=A\boldsymbol x
$$

The displayed relationship is the main object to analyse. Specify the relevant dimensions, quantities and assumptions before using it. It should be read as a mathematical statement, not merely a programming shorthand.

## Work through an original example

Let T(d,n)=2d+3n. Then T((1,1)+(2,1))=T(3,2)=12, while T(1,1)+T(2,1)=5+7=12. The intercept in f(d,n)=3+2d+3n breaks strict linearity; that function is affine.

## What follows, and what does not

A matrix represents a linear map once the domain and target bases are fixed. Composition of maps corresponds to matrix multiplication with dimensions in the correct order.

## Test your reasoning

Test T(x)=Ax+c with a nonzero c at the zero vector. Why is it generally not linear?
